subject: Follow-up: capacity pricing scenarios & cost-per-1M token anchors
messages:
From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@brightwell.com>, Amit Shah <amit.shah@brightwell.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: capacity pricing scenarios & cost-per-1M token anchors

Samantha / Amit — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and clear next steps so we can get you an apples-to-apples set of priced options for a Dedicated deployment:

1) Usage profile (your input):
- Steady inference baseline ~200M tokens/month during pilot; expected growth to ~1.1B tokens/month within 9–12 months if retention/feature adoption hits our forecast.
- Workload: mixed chat + few long-form generations (average seq length ~550 tokens).
- Latency target: p95 generation latency <400ms for short chats, <1.2s for long-form; throughput target approx 12k tokens/sec sustained across the pool.

2) Budget & unit-econ guidance (you mentioned ranges):
- Budget band you signaled: $25k–$75k/month for initial committed capacity (pilot to early production).
- You asked for target $/1M tokens anchors — we should give low/medium/high anchor scenarios so you can see tradeoffs.

3) GPU & sizing preferences discussed:
- Preference for H100-class for model X (higher throughput) but open to A100 mix for lower list prices if unit economics align.
- Want the proposal to show both: an H100-optimized lane (smaller GPU count, higher per-GPU throughput) and an A100-heavy lane (more GPUs, lower per-unit throughput).

Next steps (action items):
- Karthik + Marissa: can you produce two priced scenarios (pilot ~200M tokens/mo and production ~1.1B tokens/mo) with explicit $/1M-token anchors, reserved GPU counts, expected sustained throughput, and overage policy? Please attach an XLS with the assumptions.
- Ben: include the unit-econ assumptions (batching, KV cache hit rate, quantization option effects) that change the $/1M.
- Samantha/Amit: confirm whether the budget band above is accurate and if there are procurement/contract milestones we should plan for.

I'll assemble this into a single follow-up doc. Attaching the Brightwell RFP summary you shared and we will return a priced XLS.

Thanks,
— Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Brightwell-RFP-summary.pdf (pdf)

From: Amit Shah <amit.shah@brightwell.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@brightwell.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 17:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: capacity pricing scenarios & cost-per-1M token anchors

Thanks Lauren — that summary is useful. A couple clarifications from our side before you price: 
- The $25k–$75k/month band is correct for committed spend we can sign up to for the pilot -> early-prod window.
- Our target price per 1M tokens we'd be comfortable with: ideally under $12/1M at pilot scale, and sub-$8/1M at the 1B/month scale range.
- For hardware preference: we like the H100 option if it materially reduces the $/1M at scale, but procurement may push back on higher per-GPU line items — show both so we can take to purchasing.

Quick note: we need clarity on SLA (uptime + p95 latency SLO) and the standard overage calculation if we go over committed tokens in a month.

Samantha will coordinate internal procurement timelines.

— Amit
Director, ML Platform — Brightwell Health
amit.shah@brightwell.com

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Follow-up: capacity pricing scenarios & cost-per-1M token anchors

Looping in pricing. Danielle, see note below (cc list). I'm proposing we prepare two clean scenarios in the XLS with line items for reserved GPUs, expected usable tokens/month, and an explicit $/1M-anchor. High level draft numbers here to agree internally before we send to Brightwell: 

Scenario A — H100-optimized (target production)- Pilot (200M tokens/mo): 6 x H100 reserved GPUs (single region), monthly commit $38,000 -> implied $/1M = $190/1M? (typo — see corrected below)- Production (1.1B tokens/mo): 18 x H100 reserved GPUs, monthly commit $210,000 -> implied $/1M ≈ $191 (this also looks off)

Hold up — raw GPU price -> token $ math here is sensitive to batching/kv cache assumptions. Ben, I want you to drop the detailed unit-econ in and correct the anchors. My goal: show realistic anchors: pilot ~$40–60/1M and production ~$6–9/1M depending on quantization and caching. Those ranges align with other prospects at similar scale.

Action: Marissa, build the XLS with two hardware mixes (H100-heavy, A100-mix) and include these columns: gpu_type, gpu_count, reserved_monthly_price, estimated_token_capacity/month, implied_$per_1M, latency_assumptions, overage_rate.

We should be careful not to commit to exact $/1M in email — provide ranges and call out assumptions.

— Karthik
Sr. Account Exec (Capacity Sales), Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Follow-up: Follow-up: capacity pricing scenarios & cost-per-1M token anchors

Adding the unit-econ assumptions we will publish in the XLS so Brightwell sees the levers: 
- Batching: assumed effective tokens-per-inference = 1.8x for chat workload; higher for long-form where we can do longer prefix batching.
- KV cache: assume 30% hit rate for sessionized chat; each percentage point of additional cache hit reduces token compute by ~0.8%.
- Quantization path: FP16 (baseline) vs 4-bit quant (experimental) — quantization can improve throughput by 20–40% on H100-like kernels; show reduced $/1M under quantized path as an optional line.
- Overhead: infra and network margin 12% on top of compute costs; we will include reserved vs burst capacity pricing.

Proposed anchor outputs (internal, to be refined in XLS):
- Pilot 200M tokens/mo: H100 scenario -> implied $/1M = $48–$63 (range driven by cache/batching); A100-mix -> $62–$85/1M.
- Production 1.1B tokens/mo: H100 scenario -> implied $/1M = $5.8–$8.6; A100-mix -> $8.2–$12.4.

I'll attach a worked sheet with the per-GPU reserved line items and the sensitivity toggles. Marissa: please finalize and we'll send to Lauren to share.

Ben Carter
Senior Pricing Analyst, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachments: Redwood-dedicated-pricing.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@brightwell.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Amit Shah <amit.shah@brightwell.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: capacity pricing scenarios & cost-per-1M token anchors

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround and the ranges. A few asks from procurement before we review the numbers with Finance: 
- Please include a short summary page that calls out the baseline assumptions so we can map our expected behavior to the $/1M ranges (very helpful for procurement).
- Call out SLA SLOs (uptime %, p95 latency targets per model class) and the overage billing formula (flat per-1M overage vs blended).
- Can you show a short example month where we spike +40% above committed — how is overage calculated and what is the expected bill?

We'll review the XLS and the worked example; if the anchors on the H100 production line come in near the lower end of your ranges (~$6–8/1M), procurement will be much more favorable to H100. We'll aim to get back with a preferred scenario by Friday.

— Samantha
VP, Engineering — Brightwell Health
samantha.lee@brightwell.com
